newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Korona ups share of stocks in balanced fund.
newsitem.headline: Polish Korona ups share of stocks in balanced fund.

text.p: Polish mutual fund company Korona SA increased the share of stocks in its balanced fund's portfolio to 55.2 percent at the end of last year from 44.3 percent at the end of 1995, the company said.
The company said in a financial statement for 1996 that the share of bonds in its portfolio shrank to 14.9 percent from 18.4 percent and that T-bills dipped to 24.4 percent from 32.7.
Other assets rose to 4.8 percent from 4.4 percent and interest from bonds remained below one percent. @
Last September Korona said that at mid-year stocks made up 50.1 percent of the balanced fund's portfolio, bonds 15.9 percent, T-bills 30.5 percent and other assets 2.1 percent.
In the 1996 report Korona reiterated its statement made in January that it had increased the net asset value of its balanced fund unit last year by 59.8 percent to 81.55 zlotys.
The report said the fund's net assets rose to 52.3 million zlotys at the end of 1996 from 16.3 million at the end of 1995.
Korona's balanced fund had assets of 36.1 million zlotys at mid-year.

The balanced fund, which started selling units in August 1995, lifted operating profit to 13.3 million zlotys last year from 259,782 zlotys in 1995, with operating costs rising last year to 1.4 million zlotys from 227,160 zlotys in 1995.
Operating profit was at 7.6 million zlotys at mid-year.
Korona's main stocks at the end of last year were Sokolow, Optimus and BPH, making up 4.97 percent, 4.52 percent and 4.12 percent of its portfolio respectively.
Stomil Olsztyn came next with 3.67 percent followed by Polifarb Wroclaw with 3.61 percent. @

Korona is a joint venture between Creditanstalt Securities SA, the Polish broking subsidiary of Austria's Creditanstalt- Bankverein CABV_a.VI, and Polish state-controlled agricultural bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ).
It currently also runs an an equity and money-market fund.
